title: Patent Drafting and Prosecution
subtitle: Draft a specification that survives examination, then prosecute it: read the FER, amend the claims, argue Section 3 and prepare for the hearing.
summary: Claims first, specification second, prosecution third. Ten modules on real disclosures and real First Examination Reports, from mechanical to software to pharma.
outcomes: Draft a complete specification: field, background, summary, detailed description, claims and abstract, in that order of difficulty
Write an independent claim with the minimum essential features, and dependent claims that give you real fallback positions
Read a First Examination Report line by line and classify every objection by the response it needs
Respond to novelty and inventive-step objections by distinguishing D1 and D2 on the record, not by assertion
Argue Section 3(k) and Section 3(d) in the structure the Patent Office currently accepts
Amend claims under Sections 57 and 59 without broadening them, and show the basis in the specification
Prepare written submissions and an oral strategy for a hearing under Rule 28
Run the formal side: Form 3 updates, Form 18, Form 4 extensions, and the deadlines that cannot be extended
about: Most patent training in India teaches you what the Patents Act says. This course teaches you to write claims, because everything else in the file exists to support them, and to defend those claims when the examiner comes back with D1, D2 and a Section 3(k) objection.

You will draft three full claim sets and one complete specification, then prosecute two real applications from FER to hearing. The disclosures are from mechanical, software and pharmaceutical matters, so you see how the same method bends to each field.
This is the longest course we run, and the most demanding. Budget two drafting hours for every hour of video.

Engineers and scientists preparing for the patent agent examination who want the practical half
In-house counsel at product companies who instruct outside patent counsel
Litigators who need to read a prosecution history properly
notFor: You have never read a claim and are not willing to read fifty
You want a bar-exam style survey of patent law
You need PCT or foreign prosecution strategy; this is India-first

faq.q: Do I need a technical degree?
faq.a: No, but you need to be comfortable reading technical descriptions. The mechanical and software examples are chosen to be understandable with care rather than expertise.

faq.q: Does this prepare me for the patent agent exam?
faq.a: It prepares you for Paper II, the drafting paper, better than anything else we know of. It does not cover Paper I, which tests the Act and Rules.
